title: Low End-to-End Latency atop a Speculative Shared Log with Fix-Ante Ordering
problem: Shared log-based systems for distributed databases face latency challenges due to coordination overhead and ordering requirements; speculative execution can reduce latency but requires robust ordering guarantees.
motivation: Reducing end-to-end latency in replicated systems enables lower latency transaction processing without sacrificing consistency.
method: The system pre-assigns the sequence of database operations using 'Fix-Ante' ordering, eliminating the slow coordination normally needed with a shared log (a record all nodes check to stay synchronized). Servers then speculatively execute these pre-ordered operations (running them before full coordination completes). Each server independently verifies whether its speculative execution matched the pre-assigned order, correcting any conflicts. This delivers the speed of speculation while maintaining the consistency guarantees that distributed databases require.
key_novelty: Fix-Ante ordering lets servers speculatively execute database operations without coordination overhead by pre-assigning their order, achieving low latency while guaranteeing correctness.
contributions: Fix-Ante ordering protocol for speculative execution
Low end-to-end latency without sacrificing consistency
limitations: Effectiveness depends on speculation accuracy; high contention scenarios may reduce benefits.
primary_theme: Speculative shared log for low latency
